chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifa'ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man and the woman who die and have not performed Hajj, is the Hajj of Islam fulfilled on their behalf? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim who meets the conditions
key_terms.يَقْضِي: To fulfill or settle a debt/obligation

ai.seo_question: Does a deceased person who died without performing Hajj need to have Hajj performed on their behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi confirms the permissibility of performing Hajjat al-Islam (the obligatory Hajj) on behalf of a deceased parent or relative who died without fulfilling this pillar. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the debt of worship remains actionable by heirs or others, ensuring the spiritual obligation is settled even after death.
